candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as malware with probability 0.99. All 20 top n-grams have positive SHAP contributions toward cryptojacking, ranging from +0.0056 to +0.0109, so no feature in the evidence argues against that verdict. The n-grams fall into two groups that match the computational profile of mining or hashing code. The first is rotate-and-arithmetic sequences: ADD ROR (+0.010421, freq 0.001323), ROL AND (+0.008482), MOV ROL (+0.008449, freq 0.001502), ROL ADD (+0.008228), ROR MOV (+0.006762), XOR ROL (+0.006435, freq 0.005439, the most frequent in the list), ROL MOV (+0.005886), ADD ROL (+0.005620, freq 0.002166), SHL OR (+0.005910) and ROL MOVZX (+0.006785). Dense rotate/XOR/add chains are typical of ARX-style hash rounds such as those used in proof-of-work algorithms. The second group is SIMD sequences: PXOR MOVAPS (+0.010920, the top feature), PXOR PXOR (+0.008471), MOVDQA PAND (+0.007816), PADDQ MOVDQA (+0.007522), MOVDQU PAND (+0.006817), MOVD PUNPCKLDQ (+0.006812) and ADD MOVQ (+0.009612). These suggest vectorized 64-bit integer and bitwise operations, consistent with optimized hashing or memory-hard mining kernels. SUB ADC (+0.006907) points to multi-precision arithmetic, and BSWAP LEA (+0.006135) to endianness conversion common in hash input/output handling. CALL RET (+0.006765, freq 0.000002) is a minor structural pattern and adds little on its own. The evidence supplies no function names or API information, so the conclusion rests on instruction-level patterns alone. Because many independent features agree and the model probability is very high, the evidence supports high confidence. Legitimate cryptographic or compression software can produce similar patterns, so confirmation by further analysis is still warranted.
